title: Drifters
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Mortally wounded at the Battle of Sekigahara, samurai Shimazu Toyohisa is sent through a corridor of doors into a fantasy world of elves, dwarves and dragons. There, warriors from across history, the 'Drifters', are gathered to fight the 'Ends', another group of historical figures leading monsters to wipe out humanity.
life_message: It presents war, conquest and warrior honor as the stage on which people prove what they are worth.

content.note: Endless bloody war between historical warriors (Wikipedia synopsis, Dark Horse blurb 'bloody melee'); AniList War 100%; MU War, Genocide, Execution.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Toyohisa's Shimazu code demands answering insult and dying well (Wikipedia synopsis; AniList Samurai) (to verify).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Drifters act freely but rally under Nobunaga's leadership (to verify).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Clan loyalty mixes with new bonds among warriors of many eras (AniList Historical).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Military rank and command matter; Nobunaga plans as a lord (MU Strategic Minds, Conqueror/s).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Warrior tradition sits beside gunpowder and modern tactics (AniList Anachronism).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: A war of survival against extermination by the Ends (Wikipedia synopsis).

folkways.japan: The Shimazu samurai ethos, Sengoku-era lordship and honor in death reflect Japanese warrior tradition, here mixed with world history and Western fantasy.

delivery.evidence: No source addresses delivery; warrior honor carried by battles between Drifters and Ends (to verify).
delivery.note: Warrior honor is carried by the battles, with the Ends as forces seeking humanity's destruction.

winners_losers: The Drifters, especially Toyohisa and Nobunaga, get sympathy as defenders of the humans and enslaved elves; the Ends seek total destruction.
